text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today after climbing nearly 16% over the past two weeks, driven largely by a geopolitical shock: Trump's announced deal to import Russian diesel into the U.S. market. This directly threatens refiner margins—the profit spread between crude oil costs and fuel selling prices—because it floods the market with cheap supply precisely when refiners have benefited from tight fuel inventories and high prices caused by Middle East and Eastern Europe conflicts. The company had rallied hard on expectations that these supply disruptions would keep fuel scarce and profitable for U.S. refiners; news of Russian diesel flowing in undercuts that thesis.

The broader picture is messier, though: even with the Russian diesel deal announced, multiple other supply shocks remain active—Hurricane Isaias is disrupting Gulf production and threatening refineries, tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are creating transport risk, and U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity with global oil trading at a $29 premium to U.S. prices. The stock's retreat is likely profit-taking after a sharp run-up, mixed with disappointment that a major new supply source could relieve the fuel scarcity that had been propping up refiner economics.
